non_blocking_items.title: Decoded-result binding is by value and remains an operator precondition
non_blocking_items.detail: The runner seals raw/metadata/windows SHAs in result['perf_switch_capture']['outputs'] and names the expected consumer output ('perf-decoded.json'), and the consumer echoes its input SHAs. No executed check compares the two. Because the formal gate rejects the marker outright, this cannot promote diagnostic evidence, but an operator who wants provenance should compare the values by hand or with a small post-run check.
non_blocking_items.suggested_minimal_fix: Document the compare step in the delivery entry, or add a pure helper that fails closed when report.inputs.raw_sha256 != marker.outputs.raw.sha256 (no shared-ledger change).

non_blocking_items.title: tools/audit_mixed_control.py deliberately does not flag perf_switch_capture
non_blocking_items.detail: The flight audit contains no 'perf' reference and its 'Unexpected alternate workflow' loop omits perf_switch_capture, so an instrumented archive can still receive audit status='pass'. This is intentional (the raw audit must remain usable for instrumented flights) and formality is guaranteed only by joint_profile._mixed_proofs. A reader must not treat the raw audit pass as formal MIXED/PV admission.
non_blocking_items.suggested_minimal_fix: No code change required. If desired, add a limitations line to the audit report naming the diagnostic marker; avoid touching shared tooling otherwise.

non_blocking_items.title: Consumer --windows is optional while the runner always seals perf-windows.json
non_blocking_items.detail: The consumer accepts a capture without --windows and then reports windows=null. The intended procedure (run with --windows and require a non-empty intersection) is documented but not enforced by the tool.
non_blocking_items.suggested_minimal_fix: Keep as-is; the operator procedure already requires --windows. Optionally add a test that a missing windows file is a caller error in the delivery script, not in the consumer.

non_blocking_items.title: stream_completeness_proven is derived from sealed metadata, not an independent native re-read
non_blocking_items.detail: validate_kernel_loss_counter accepts read_ok=true, read_bytes=16, errno=0, count=0 and config.read_format=16 as proof. This is a configuration-level completeness assertion scoped by the consumer's own scope string; it is not an independent measurement of CPU execution or causal scheduling.
non_blocking_items.suggested_minimal_fix: None required. Keep the scope/limitations text with the decoded artifact.

non_blocking_items.title: strict_consumer_passed is permanently False in this runner
non_blocking_items.detail: By design: the runner only seals outputs for an external consumer. Readers must branch on presence of the perf_switch_capture key (as the formal gate does), never on the boolean, or on the raw audit status alone.

failure.cause: OSError WinError 1314: the Windows host lacks the privilege to create a symlink; the failing line is outside the admission chain
failure.classification: environment-only, non-blocking; expected to pass on Linux/WSL where symlink creation is permitted

shipped_perf_admission_tests.command: pytest -k 'perf or marker or mixed_result or strict or reject or seal or lifecycle'

verdict: The 'diagnostic evidence is never promoted to formal evidence' chain holds at HEAD 100ef1a: the formal MIXED/PV gate rejects perf_switch_capture by key presence for every value shape, before the raw-evidence walk; the runner never self-certifies the strict consumer and never executes it; extra perf sources keep source-set identity; a failed or absent strict consumer cannot be recorded as a pass. No blocking items; five non-blocking notes recorded above.
